candidates.name: Sphenoid sinusitis
support_spans: 6 months of progressive right mandibular pain radiating to the zygomatic and mastoid regions
enlargement of the right sphenoid sinus with overdevelopment and opacity of the lateral recess
purulent discharge in the sphenoethmoidal recess
persistent inflammation of the sphenoid sinus, skull base, and pterygoid fossa
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are consistent with sphenoid sinusitis, which is an inflammation of the sphenoid sinus.

candidates.name: Trigeminal neuralgia
support_spans: progressive right mandibular pain radiating to the zygomatic and mastoid regions
contradict_spans: An empirical course of prednisone (50 mg per day) for presumed trigeminal neuralgia provided no benefit
candidates.why: The patient's pain pattern is consistent with trigeminal neuralgia, but the lack of response to prednisone and other findings suggest that it may not be the primary diagnosis.

candidates.name: Pyocycle
support_spans: the sphenoid ostium was obstructed by a pyocele, which was marsupialized and drained
candidates.why: The presence of a pyocele, which is a collection of pus, is consistent with an infectious process such as sphenoid sinusitis.

candidates.name: Tolosa-Hunt syndrome
support_spans: progressive right mandibular pain radiating to the zygomatic and mastoid regions
infiltrating the V2 and V3 trigeminal branches; intracranial extension into the cavernous sinus surrounded the Gasserian ganglion
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are consistent with Tolosa-Hunt syndrome, a rare disorder characterized by painful ophthalmoplegia caused by nonspecific inflammation of the cavernous sinus or superior orbital fissure.

candidates.name: Sphenoid sinus mucocele
support_spans: enlargement of the right sphenoid sinus with overdevelopment and opacity of the lateral recess
pyocele, which was marsupialized and drained
candidates.why: The patient's imaging findings and surgical results are consistent with a sphenoid sinus mucocele, a benign condition characterized by an accumulation of mucous secretion within the sphenoid sinus.

candidates.name: Chronic invasive fungal sinusitis
support_spans: purulent discharge in the sphenoethmoidal recess
persistent inflammation of the sphenoid sinus, skull base, and pterygoid fossa
contradict_spans: Histopathology was negative for hyphae and neoplastic cells, and cultures grew no bacteria or fungi
candidates.why: Despite the negative histopathology and cultures, the patient's clinical presentation and imaging findings could still be consistent with chronic invasive fungal sinusitis, a rare and aggressive condition that requires a high index of suspicion for diagnosis.
